state_at_read.days_lost: ROOT CAUSE FOUND: not a broken route. The Hermes cron jobs arc-fire-next-arm (10:05 local) and arc-fire-next-arm-b (10:25 local) ran every day and completed in 5-20 s, but from 2026-10-01 on they had NOTHING TO FIRE: every arm in scripts/arm-queue.json (v17, v18, v15, v16, harness-gemma, augment20, v11-redraw-11, redraw3, redraw4) had its message already present in the submissions list, so select() returned None and the route exited 0 -- a graceful no-op that reads exactly like a healthy run in the execution log (status completed, delivery suppressed). 2026-09-30 was therefore the last fired round and 10-01..10-03 are three lost, unbankable UTC days on both boards. Fix applied this round: two fresh arms re-armed at the head of the queue (duck-sota-redraw1 for AGI-3, v11-redraw-12 for AGI-2), so the route has something to advance on 10-05.

environment_facts.kernel_slug: A kernel's id must equal the slug Kaggle derives from its title. Pushing id uts3125025522741/arc-agi-3-duck-sota with title 'ARC AGI 3 duck sota (open-source lift)' printed a warning and created uts3125025522741/arc-agi-3-duck-sota-open-source-lift; the id in kernel-metadata.json was corrected to that slug so the next push makes a version, not a second kernel.
environment_facts.kernels_status_ref: kernels status wants the created slug, not the metadata id -- the metadata id answers 'Permission kernels.get was denied', which reads like a wrong slug rather than a mismatched one.
environment_facts.cron_no_op_is_silent: A drained arm queue makes the unattended route a successful no-op, not a failure: it exits 0 in 5-20 s and the cron ledger records status=completed. Nothing in the execution record distinguishes it from a round that fired. Only the submissions table shows the gap (last fire 2026-09-30 while the jobs ran daily).
